status: research concepts only; no replacement selected or CAD implemented
user_direction: Develop Option A sliding-plunger alternatives; investigate phone-button return without rubber bands.
recommendation: A1 first, with provision for optional A4 return leaves
orientation: Schematic side projections, press toward phone downward; depth offsets are not dimensioned.
concepts: A1 centered pull and fixed-axis rotating pulley
A2 centered pull and fixed rounded eye
A3 moving pulley with 2:1 stroke reduction
A4 A1 plus paired printed return leaves
return_condition: Button restoring force must exceed slider stiction, reflected cord/pulley resistance, residual input tension and adverse gravity throughout release. Button cannot restore a positive air gap by itself.
common_requirements: Short separated guide lands and relieved non-bearing surfaces
Settable gap independent of twine knot
Frame stop adjusted to measured button travel
Separate input travel accommodation; a hard stop alone is insufficient
excess_pull_candidate: A replaceable printed flexure at trigger-side twine attachment could take up remaining trigger displacement after the slider stop engages. Its stroke and force rise must be designed from measurements. This is not a constant-force limiter and must not bottom out in normal travel.
unknowns: Actual phone model/case and return-force curve
Trigger cord travel and residual tension

sources.title: igus: eccentric drive loads and binding
sources.finding: Keep the drive near the guide axis and avoid overconstraining parallel guides. Their numeric 2:1 rule is specific to their bearings, not a PLA design limit.

sources.title: OMRON: tactile switch precautions
sources.finding: Straight actuation and avoidance of excess force after the switch stops. General design guidance only: not an iPhone switch specification.

sources.title: MIT: capstan friction
sources.finding: Cord sliding around a fixed surface incurs friction; unknown twine/PLA friction prevents a numerical return prediction.

sources.title: Sava: pulley design
sources.finding: Pulley bend diameter matters. Published wire-rope diameter ratios must not be transferred to unspecified textile twine.

sources.title: Sharkey et al.: printed flexure translation stage
sources.finding: Printed flexures are a demonstrated mechanism family. This does not validate these leaf dimensions or lifetime.

sources.title: Fischbach and Weinberg: flexural creep of printed PLA
sources.finding: PLA flexural creep and aging are experimentally relevant; permanent spring preload needs validation.
